docs.title: My Note
docs.text:
Welcome to the documentation and thank you for checking out World Journal.

I wanted one place where I could explore what is happening around the world, keep the sources visible and write down the things I did not want to forget. I could not find an app that handled those parts together in the way I wanted, so I built this one.

World Journal is intentionally local and personal. It does not need an account, a paid API or a separate frontend service. Your journal and settings stay on the machine running the app, while news articles and videos still open at their original sources.

I use the app myself and plan to keep improving it. It is not trying to become a large hosted platform. It is simply meant to be useful, understandable and dependable for people who want this particular kind of research space.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: On this page I will explain the high-level flow of World Journal and the choices behind how it stores and refreshes information.

docs.title: 1. Where the Data Comes From
docs.text:
The country catalog and map geometry are bundled with the app from a pinned Natural Earth dataset. Country facts are also bundled as reviewed snapshots rather than fetched every time a page opens.

Current news comes from external feeds:

  • Google News RSS for broad country and world searches;
  • RSS or Atom feeds published by regional news organizations;
  • public YouTube channel feeds for recent videos.

The app stores normalized metadata from those feeds. It does not scrape full articles, bypass paywalls or download videos. Selecting an article opens the original result or publisher page.

docs.title: 2. Local Storage
docs.text:
Personal data is saved in a local SQLite database. Uploaded journal images are stored in the local media/ folder.

This includes entries, collections, country tags, favorites, map presets, source preferences and custom territory edits. No external personal-data service is involved.

Optional authentication uses a Django administrator account as one gate around the whole installation. It does not create separate data for each account. Everyone who is allowed into one installation shares the same journal and settings.

Some presentation choices belong only to the current browser. Themes, the home country, map display settings and player position use browser storage so two browsers can keep different layouts while sharing the same journal.

docs.title: 3. Feed Refreshing
docs.text:
A bounded scheduler runs inside Django while the server is active. It refreshes enabled feeds in the background with a small worker pool.

The normal refresh interval is 12 hours plus a separate random 1 to 30 minutes for each feed before it becomes due. That random time is not a delay inserted between every download. Missing feeds and manual refresh requests can start promptly.

When a country is selected, its missing or due feeds receive priority. Existing cached content remains usable when a provider temporarily fails. Repeated failures back off instead of retrying continuously.

Note: The scheduler is intentionally part of the Django process. World Journal does not require Celery, Redis or a separate worker service.

docs.title: 4. Page Memory
docs.text:
World Journal uses Django templates and HTMX rather than a separate frontend application. Normal URLs still work directly, while top-level navigation replaces only the main content area.

The browser retains one Map, Journal, News and Countries workspace. This is why the map canvas, camera, selected country, loaded tabs, reading position and unsaved Journal form can survive a trip to another section.

The video player and notifications belong to the persistent shell outside that replaced area. A full refresh still starts a new browser workspace and stops the current video.

docs.title: 5. Reliability and Longevity
docs.text:
External feeds can move, fail or change format. They are kept behind adapters and source configuration so one provider does not define the entire app.

The parts that matter most are local. A feed shutting down does not remove saved Journal entries, local images, favorites or presets. The app may need a new source configuration, but your explicit research remains on your machine and can be exported in a portable backup.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text: On this page I will describe the main parts of World Journal and the details that are useful when you start building your own research collection.

docs.title: 1. Map
docs.text: The Map is the main way to explore the app. Select a country to open its drawer, then move between Overview, Articles, Videos and Notes without losing the selected country.

docs.title: 1.1 Map Types
docs.text:
World Journal has three map types:

  • Terrain uses the configured external map style for familiar geographic detail.
  • Simple uses bundled country geometry and removes roads, buildings and other unnecessary layers.
  • Adventure turns the world into an illustrated maritime atlas with its own colors, textures and artwork.

Your map type, camera position and display choices are remembered by the browser.

docs.title: 1.2 Country Overview
docs.text:
Overview shows bundled facts such as the capital, population, area, languages, currency and government when those facts are available. The facts are stored with the app, so opening an Overview does not make a live request to a facts service.

The map contains 238 ISO-backed entries and 14 custom territories from the pinned Natural Earth dataset. Custom territories can have their details edited locally. Their X identifiers belong only to World Journal and are not official ISO assignments.

docs.title: 1.3 Articles and Videos
docs.text:
Articles combines a Google News country search with matching stories from enabled regional feeds. Videos uses public YouTube channel feeds. Every item keeps its publisher or channel visible.

A source can fail without making the whole country drawer fail. If a previous successful result exists, the app can continue showing that cached result with a warning.

Note: Matching is a useful filter, not a claim that every relevant story was found. Regional items are matched through reviewed country names and aliases rather than by downloading article bodies.

docs.title: 1.4 Favorites and Presets
docs.text:
Favorite countries from the drawer so they are easier to recognize and revisit. Favorites are shared data stored in SQLite.

Color presets let you create named country groups, assign colors and add group titles for the legend. The preset editor also lets you select countries directly on the map.

docs.title: 2. Journal
docs.text: The Journal is the permanent research space. News cache and archives can expire, but entries you explicitly save remain until you delete them.

docs.title: 2.1 Entries and Collections
docs.text:
An entry can be a Note, Article, Video or Bookmark. New saves are placed into the matching automatic collection unless you choose another collection.

Entries support:

  • Markdown text;
  • ordered subsections;
  • one or more country tags;
  • article and video references;
  • YouTube timestamps;
  • event dates;
  • local images;
  • favorite and pinned states.

docs.title: 2.2 Writing and Autosave
docs.text:
While editing an existing entry, changed content autosaves approximately once per minute. The status near the editor tells you whether the current version is saved. Explicit Save buttons remain available when you want to finish immediately.

Valid YouTube links written in Markdown become player controls. They do not create automatic third-party iframes inside the entry.

docs.title: 2.3 Country References
docs.text:
Use [[Romania]] or another exact country name in Markdown to create a country link. Known aliases and canonical names are resolved when the entry is saved. Unrecognized text remains visible instead of being guessed.

Country statistics use explicit country relationships. A country name appearing in ordinary prose does not silently change the statistics.

docs.title: 2.4 Search, Filters and Statistics
docs.text: The Journal can be searched and filtered by collection, entry type, country, event date, creation date and favorite state. Statistics summarize entries by type, collection, country and time period, and the totals link back to the relevant filtered list.

docs.title: 3. News
docs.text: The News page provides a broader reading board outside a single country drawer. Use its tabs and filters to move between current results and the rolling archive.

docs.title: 3.1 Sources
docs.text:
World Journal supports:

  • Google News country and world RSS searches;
  • curated RSS and Atom feeds;
  • public YouTube channel feeds;
  • custom RSS feeds and YouTube channels added in Settings.

Go to Settings > Sources to enable or disable sources, add custom ones, inspect health and request a refresh.

docs.title: 3.2 Archive
docs.text:
Article and video metadata is kept in a rolling 90-day archive. The archive is bounded to 50,000 items and an approximate 100 MiB metadata budget. It does not download article bodies, publisher pages or video files.

Save anything important to the Journal rather than relying on the archive as permanent storage.

docs.title: 4. Countries
docs.text:
Countries provides a searchable and sortable directory of the same places used by the Map and Journal. Favorites appear in their own section, and each country has larger Overview, Articles, Videos and Notes views.

Selecting a custom territory exposes Edit details in Overview. Local edits can change its display name and facts without changing its stable identifier or existing relationships.

docs.title: 5. Video Player
docs.text:
Press Play on a supported YouTube item to load it into the shared player. The iframe is only created after that action and uses the privacy-enhanced YouTube domain.

The player can be moved, minimized, expanded and closed. It lives outside the page area replaced during navigation, so the same video can continue while you move between Map, Journal, News, Countries and Settings.

Use the bookmark control to save the current video and continue writing in the Journal.

docs.title: 6. Settings
docs.text:
Settings is divided into Preferences, Backup, Sources and Information.

  • Preferences controls the theme, home country, map type and map labels.
  • Backup exports or imports portable personal data.
  • Sources controls feeds, channels, refresh timing and source health.
  • Information collects application and data-source information.

Themes and visual map preferences belong to the current browser. Journal entries, favorites, presets, source choices and territory edits are shared through SQLite.

docs.title: The Page Has No Styling
docs.text:
The Problem:

The app loads through runserver or Waitress but CSS, JavaScript or map assets return errors.

The Cause:

Static files were not collected after installation or an update.

The Solution:

WindowsMac and Linux 
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe manage.py collectstatic --noinput

.venv/bin/python manage.py collectstatic --noinput

Restart the server and hard refresh the browser.

docs.title: Login Keeps Rejecting the Account
docs.text:
The Problem:

Authentication is enabled but the login page rejects the username or password.

The Cause:

The administrator account may not exist in the same SQLite database used by the running process. This is common when createsuperuser was run outside the container or with a different WORLD_JOURNAL_DATA_DIR.

The Solution:

For Docker, create the account inside the running container:

docker exec -it world-journal python manage.py createsuperuser

For a native install, use the project's .venv interpreter from the project folder. Confirm that the server and the command use the same environment variables.

docs.title: The Cache Table Does Not Exist
docs.text:
The Problem:

The app reports an error mentioning world_journal_cache when trying to read or refresh news.

The Cause:

The one-time database cache setup was skipped.

The Solution:

Stop the server and run:

WindowsMac and Linux 
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe manage.py createcachetable world_journal_cache

.venv/bin/python manage.py createcachetable world_journal_cache

Run the command again after replacing the database with a fresh empty one.

docs.title: Static Changes Do Not Appear
docs.text:
The Problem:

The server restarted but the map, styles or controls still look unchanged.

The Cause:

The browser is using cached CSS or JavaScript.

The Solution:

Restart Django and use a hard refresh. On Windows and Linux press Ctrl+F5. On Mac use Command+Shift+R.

docs.title: News Is Empty or Stale
docs.text:
The Problem:

A country has no recent articles or shows a refresh warning.

The Cause:

A publisher feed may be unavailable, rate limited or waiting for its next scheduled refresh. The scheduler only runs while Django is running.

The Solution:

Open Settings > Sources and inspect the source health. Use the manual refresh action once, then allow the background queue time to work. Repeatedly pressing refresh does not bypass provider limits.

Cached stories may remain visible after a failure. A failure from one source should not hide successful results from another source.

docs.title: The Map Is Blank or Incomplete
docs.text:
The Problem:

The map canvas is blank, or Terrain does not show provider detail.

The Cause:

Simple and Adventure use bundled country geometry, but Terrain and map labels can depend on external map resources. A stale browser cache can also keep an old module loaded.

The Solution:

Try Simple or Adventure first, then hard refresh. Check that the machine has internet access before using Terrain. If bundled map files are missing, update the repository rather than generating new geometry during ordinary setup.

docs.title: A YouTube Video Will Not Play
docs.text:
The Problem:

The player reports that the video is unavailable or embedding is disabled.

The Cause:

Publishers can disable embedded playback, remove a video or restrict it by region. World Journal cannot override those choices.

The Solution:

Use Open on YouTube in the player. Saving the video to the Journal still keeps its title, link and timestamp even when the embed cannot play.

docs.title: An Image Will Not Upload
docs.text:
The Problem:

A Journal image is rejected.

The Cause:

Images are checked by their real file content, size and dimensions. Renaming an unsupported file extension does not turn it into a valid image.

The Solution:

Use a valid JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF no larger than 10 MiB. Re-export unusually large or damaged images before uploading them again.

docs.title: A Journal Draft Looks Unsaved
docs.text:
The Problem:

The editor status does not say Saved.

The Cause:

Autosave runs approximately once per minute and can fail because of validation or a lost connection.

The Solution:

Keep the editor open, correct any visible form errors and press Save. Do not refresh or close the tab until the status confirms the entry was saved.

docs.title: An Import Cannot Be Confirmed
docs.text:
The Problem:

A backup import stops during preview or reports an invalid archive.

The Cause:

World Journal validates the backup version, paths, manifest and attachment checksums before writing data.

The Solution:

Use the original ZIP created by World Journal. Do not extract and rebuild it with renamed files. Keep the existing database and media folder until a restore has completed successfully.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
By default World Journal does not require a login. This is convenient for local use on one computer or a trusted home network.

If you expose the app to the internet, enable the whole-app login gate. It protects every app page and uploaded journal image. There is no registration page. You create the administrator account yourself in the terminal.

The data is still shared. Authentication controls who can enter the app, but it does not create separate journals for different accounts.

docs.title: Step 1: Create an Account
docs.text:
DockerWindowsMacLinux 
docker exec -it world-journal python manage.py createsuperuser

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe manage.py createsuperuser

.venv/bin/python manage.py createsuperuser

.venv/bin/python manage.py createsuperuser

Django asks for a username, optional email and password. Nothing appears while the password is being typed.

docs.title: Step 2: Enable the Login Screen
docs.text:
Start the app with REQUIRE_LOGIN=True.

DockerWindowsMacLinux

Uncomment the variable in docker-compose.yml:

environment:
  - REQUIRE_LOGIN=True

Restart the container:

docker compose up -d

PowerShell:

$env:REQUIRE_LOGIN="True"
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:8000 --noreload

Command Prompt or a .bat file:

set REQUIRE_LOGIN=True
.venv\Scripts\python.exe manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:8000 --noreload

export REQUIRE_LOGIN=True
.venv/bin/python manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:8000 --noreload

For a LaunchAgent, add it to EnvironmentVariables:

<key>REQUIRE_LOGIN</key>
<string>True</string>

export REQUIRE_LOGIN=True
.venv/bin/python manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:8000 --noreload

For systemd, add it under [Service]:

Environment="REQUIRE_LOGIN=True"

When the setting is enabled, unauthenticated requests are redirected to /login/. Log out from the persistent header. When the setting is disabled, the login route returns to the Map and the app works without an account.

docs.title: Data and Backups
docs.text: World Journal keeps personal data on the machine running the app. There is no cloud copy to restore from, so backups matter.

docs.title: Where Data Is Stored
docs.text:
• db.sqlite3 contains journal entries, collections, country relationships, favorites, presets, source choices, the news archive and custom territory edits. Docker stores this file under runtime/.
  • media/ contains uploaded journal images.
  • Browser preferences such as the theme, home country, map type, player position and retained page state are stored in that browser.
  • world_journal_cache is a table inside SQLite used for feed snapshots. Cached news can be downloaded again and does not need to be treated as permanent data.

docs.title: Portable Backup
docs.text:
Open Settings > Backup and export a ZIP archive. The archive includes the journal, attachments, collections, country relationships, favorites, map presets, source choices and custom territory details.

Import always starts with a preview. Review what will be added, kept or reused before confirming the write.

Note: Feed cache and the rolling news archive are temporary research aids. Explicit Journal saves are the permanent record.

docs.title: Manual Backup
docs.text:
For a complete native-install copy:

  1. Stop the Django server.
  2. Copy db.sqlite3 and the entire media/ folder together.
  3. Store both copies somewhere outside the project folder.
  4. Start the server again.

Copying the database while the app is actively writing can produce an inconsistent backup, so stop the server first.

For Docker, stop the container with docker compose down, then copy runtime/db.sqlite3 and media/. Start it again with docker compose up -d.

docs.title: Remote Access
docs.text: To access World Journal away from home, you have two main options.

docs.title: Option 1: Private Access with Tailscale
docs.text:
Tailscale creates an encrypted private connection between your devices. Install it on the machine running World Journal and on each device that needs access.

  • Pros: Private, simple and does not require opening a public port.
  • Cons: Tailscale must be installed on every device.

Authentication is still recommended if more than one person or device can reach the server.

docs.title: Option 2: Public Access with a Tunnel
docs.text:
A service such as Cloudflare Tunnel can expose the app through an HTTPS domain without forwarding a router port.

Before doing this:

  1. enable Authentication;
  2. set a unique SECRET_KEY;
  3. configure CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS with the public HTTPS address;
  4. use Waitress rather than Django's development server.

docs.title: Configuring a Domain
docs.text:
CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS accepts one or more comma-separated origins. Include the https:// prefix.

DockerWindowsMacLinux 
environment:
  - REQUIRE_LOGIN=True
  - SECRET_KEY=replace-this-with-a-long-random-value
  - CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=https://your-domain.com

docker compose up -d

PowerShell:

$env:REQUIRE_LOGIN="True"
$env:SECRET_KEY="replace-this-with-a-long-random-value"
$env:CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS="https://your-domain.com"
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m waitress --listen=0.0.0.0:8000 --threads=8 config.wsgi:application

Command Prompt or a .bat file:

set REQUIRE_LOGIN=True
set SECRET_KEY=replace-this-with-a-long-random-value
set CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=https://your-domain.com
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m waitress --listen=0.0.0.0:8000 --threads=8 config.wsgi:application

export REQUIRE_LOGIN=True
export SECRET_KEY=replace-this-with-a-long-random-value
export CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=https://your-domain.com
.venv/bin/python -m waitress --listen=0.0.0.0:8000 --threads=8 config.wsgi:application

Add the variables to the systemd service:

Environment="REQUIRE_LOGIN=True"
Environment="SECRET_KEY=replace-this-with-a-long-random-value"
Environment="CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=https://your-domain.com"

Then restart it:

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl restart worldjournal

World Journal does not provide HTTPS itself. The tunnel or reverse proxy must terminate HTTPS before forwarding requests to Waitress.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: This page outlines the technologies used by World Journal and how the repository is divided.

docs.title: Tech Stack
docs.text:
World Journal is a monolithic Django application. The goal is to keep local installation understandable while still preserving a persistent map and video player in the browser.

  • Backend: Django 5.2 on Python 3.13
  • Database: SQLite
  • Templates and navigation: Django templates with HTMX partial navigation
  • Frontend: Vanilla JavaScript and CSS
  • Map: Bundled MapLibre GL JS with local Natural Earth geometry
  • Feeds: RSS and Atom through feedparser, fetched with httpx
  • Journal formatting: Markdown rendered with markdown-it-py
  • Images: Pillow validates local uploads
  • Static files: WhiteNoise serves collected CSS, JavaScript, fonts and map assets
  • Production server: Waitress serves the Django WSGI application

There is no Node build, separate frontend project, Redis, Celery or required cloud service.

docs.title: Application Structure
docs.text:
The Django apps follow the main data ownership boundaries:

  • core owns the persistent shell, top-level pages and portable backups.
  • countries owns country identity, custom territories, favorites, profiles and map presets.
  • news owns source configuration, feed adapters, caching, matching, refreshing and the rolling archive.
  • journal owns entries, collections, subsections, attachments, search and statistics.

Templates live under templates/, browser modules under static/js/, styles under static/css/ and reviewed data files under data/.

docs.title: Persistent Shell
docs.text:
templates/core/app_shell.html contains the header, #app-content, video player, notification rack and shared confirmation dialog.

HTMX replaces #app-content while normal direct URLs continue to return full documents. static/js/page_memory.js retains the latest Map, Journal, News and Countries nodes so state survives navigation without keeping an unlimited page cache.

The Map is suspended rather than destroyed while another section is visible. Returning reuses the same MapLibre canvas and camera. The shared video iframe remains outside the swap target and can continue playing.

docs.title: News Pipeline
docs.text:
Provider-specific code lives behind feed adapters. The rest of the app works with normalized article and video records.

A small scheduler in news/services/background.py starts with Django and uses bounded daemon threads. General workers refresh due feeds while a separate priority lane handles selected countries. Successful snapshots are kept in Django's database cache so stale results can remain available after a temporary failure.

The normal interval is 12 hours plus a per-feed random 1 to 30 minutes. Repeated failures back off. Google requests are paced globally, and rate limits pause Google work without stopping unrelated RSS or YouTube feeds.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Authentication is optional and disabled by default. core.middleware.GlobalLoginRequiredMiddleware checks REQUIRE_LOGIN on every request. When it is enabled, unauthenticated requests are redirected to Django's login view.

The login uses accounts created through createsuperuser; there is no registration page. The same middleware runs before the media-serving route, so uploaded Journal images are protected with the rest of the app. Authentication is one installation-wide gate, not a multi-user data model.

docs.title: Production Serving
docs.text:
WJ_DEV=True enables Django debug mode for development. Normal setup leaves debug mode off.

WhiteNoise serves the files generated by collectstatic, allowing both Django runserver and Waitress to use the same static setup. Waitress runs config.wsgi:application and requires no separate application server configuration.

Docker uses port 8091 on the host and port 8000 inside the container. SQLite and backup staging are mounted under runtime/, while uploaded images are mounted under media/. Bundled configuration in data/ remains part of the image and is never replaced by the persistence volume.

TZ selects Django's local timezone while stored timestamps remain timezone aware. CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS accepts comma-separated HTTPS origins for remote access.

docs.title: Minimal Dependencies
docs.text:
Runtime dependencies stay in requirements.txt. Documentation tools remain separate:

-r requirements.txt
mkdocs-material==9.*

Build the documentation with:

python -m mkdocs build --strict

Use python -m mkdocs serve for a local documentation preview.

docs.title: External Services
docs.text:
World Journal can browse bundled maps and facts without a live facts API. Current news and video metadata still depend on publishers, Google News, YouTube feeds and the configured Terrain map resources.

Those services are treated as replaceable inputs. Failures are scoped to the relevant section and do not remove local Journal data.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: If you want to fix a bug, improve the documentation or add a focused feature, contributions are welcome. For a large change, open an issue first so the direction can be discussed before you spend time rebuilding a major part of the app.

docs.title: Development Setup
docs.text:
Follow the setup guide for your operating system, then install the development requirements instead of the runtime file alone:

WindowsMac and Linux 
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt

.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt

Run Django from the repository root. The app uses direct source files and does not have a frontend build step.

Enable Django's development mode in the terminal used to run the server:

WindowsMac and Linux 
$env:WJ_DEV="True"

export WJ_DEV=True

docs.title: Project Rules
docs.text:
Keep changes consistent with the existing architecture:

  • use Django templates, HTMX, CSS and small vanilla JavaScript modules;
  • preserve direct URL loads and progressive enhancement;
  • keep authentication as an optional installation-wide gate unless the shared-data model is deliberately redesigned;
  • do not add a separate frontend framework, Redis or Celery without an explicit project decision;
  • keep dependencies minimal;
  • preserve the shell-owned video player and notification system;
  • preserve retained page state when changing top-level navigation;
  • use source adapters for feed-specific behavior;
  • update backup mappings when stored models change.

Adventure map artwork and country colors have their own established rendering path. Hover and selection use feature-state line layers above ordinary artwork. Do not replace that with geometry rebuilding or per-hover layer changes.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Use the workspace virtual environment for Python commands:

WindowsMac and Linux 
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe manage.py check
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe manage.py test
git diff --check

.venv/bin/python manage.py check
.venv/bin/python manage.py test
git diff --check

Tests should use local fixtures rather than depending on live news publishers.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The documentation uses Material for MkDocs, matching the structure used by Media Journal.

Preview it locally with:

WindowsMac and Linux 
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m mkdocs serve

.venv/bin/python -m mkdocs serve

When the public repository and GitHub Pages are ready, publish the site with:

python -m mkdocs gh-deploy

That command builds the site and writes the generated files to the gh-pages branch. Do not commit the local site/ build directory.

docs.title: Preparing a Release
docs.text:
Release information is maintained in config/version.py. Before publishing a release, update APP_VERSION to the new tag. The Information page uses that value for Your Release and checks the configured GitHub repository for Latest Release.

REPOSITORY_URL and LATEST_RELEASE_API_URL in the same file contain the repository placeholders. Update them if the final GitHub owner or repository name changes.

docs.title: Pull Requests
docs.text:
Keep a pull request focused on one problem. Explain what changed, mention any migrations or generated assets and include the manual checks that matter for the affected workflow.

Do not commit personal databases, uploaded media, backup staging files or virtual environments. Those paths are already ignored by Git.

docs.title: Database Schema
docs.text: World Journal uses Django's ORM with one local SQLite database. The schema keeps permanent personal research separate from temporary feed cache while allowing countries to connect the rest of the app.

docs.title: Countries
docs.text:
Country stores the stable two-character identity used by routes and relationships. The original 238 entries use ISO-backed data. The 14 additional Natural Earth areas use reviewed local X keys and set is_custom.

Key related models are:

  • TerritoryDetails stores local fact and name overrides for custom territories.
  • CountryFavorite stores shared favorites.
  • MapPreset stores each named color preset.
  • PresetCountry assigns a color to a country inside a preset.
  • PresetColorGroup stores optional group titles used by the legend.
  • MapPersonalState records which preset is active.
  • CountryProfile connects a country Overview note to the Journal.

Names are display data, not relationship keys. Editing a custom territory name does not replace its country row or break existing tags.

docs.title: Journal
docs.text:
ResearchContent contains fields shared by entries and subsections. Entry and EntrySection inherit from it so both can hold Markdown and structured references without duplicating unrelated tables.

  • Collection organizes entries.
  • Entry stores the main record, UUID, type, dates, flags and country relationships.
  • EntrySection stores ordered child sections.
  • Attachment stores metadata for uploaded local images.

Uploaded files live under media/; the database stores their relationships and metadata. Signals handle deliberate cleanup when records are removed.

docs.title: News
docs.text:
Feed snapshots use Django's world_journal_cache database table. The durable news models are used for preferences, custom sources and bounded history:

  • ArchivedNews stores normalized article or video metadata for the rolling archive.
  • ArchivedNewsSource connects archived items to their source identity.
  • ArchivedNewsCountry records country matches.
  • SourcePreference stores enabled or disabled source choices.
  • NewsPreferences stores shared refresh settings.
  • CustomSource stores user-added feeds and channels.

The archive keeps metadata only. It is limited to 90 days, 50,000 items and an approximate 100 MiB accounted metadata budget.

docs.title: Backups and Migrations
docs.text:
Django migrations are the source of truth for schema changes. Country catalog migrations also seed stable country rows that other records reference.

Portable backups use their own versioned format rather than exposing a raw database dump. Backup format 5 includes custom territory edits and remains able to read formats 1 through 4.

When adding or changing a stored model, review all of these areas together:

  1. the Django model and migration;
  2. portable export and import mappings;
  3. merge and conflict behavior;
  4. invalidation of retained browser views;
  5. documentation for any user-visible data.

docs.title: Setup for Docker
docs.text:
New to Docker? If you have not used Docker before and plan to run the app on your personal computer, check the native Windows, Mac or Linux guides instead.

  1. Clone the repository:

    ```sh
git clone https://github.com/mihail-pop/world-journal.git
cd world-journal
```

  2. Open docker-compose.yml in a text editor. Uncomment and update the TZ variable with your timezone.

    ```yaml
environment:
    - TZ=Europe/Bucharest
```

Use an IANA timezone such as `Europe/London`, `Europe/Bucharest` or `America/New_York`. If it is omitted, World Journal uses UTC.

  3. Build and start the app:

    ```sh
docker compose up -d --build
```

  4. Open http://localhost:8091.

World Journal uses port 8091 on the host so it can run next to Media Journal, which uses 8090. The container still listens on port 8000 internally.

Personal data is stored in runtime/ and uploaded images in media/. Both folders remain on the host when the container is replaced.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
From the project folder run:

git pull
docker compose up -d --build

The container applies migrations, creates the database cache table and collects static files before Waitress starts.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
If you expose the app outside a trusted local network, enable authentication by uncommenting this line in docker-compose.yml:

environment:
    - REQUIRE_LOGIN=True

Create the administrator account used to log in:

docker exec -it world-journal python manage.py createsuperuser

Read the Authentication Guide

docs.title: Remote Access
docs.text:
For a custom domain, also set a unique SECRET_KEY and add the HTTPS origin:

environment:
    - SECRET_KEY=replace-this-with-a-long-random-value
    - CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=https://your-domain.com

Read the Remote Access Guide

docs.title: Setup for Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)
docs.text:
1. Install Python, virtual environment support and Git:

    sudo apt update
sudo apt install python3 python3-pip python3-venv git

  2. Navigate to the folder where you want to keep the app, then clone the repository:

    git clone https://github.com/mihail-pop/world-journal.git
cd world-journal

  3. Create the virtual environment:

    python3 -m venv .venv

  4. Install the dependencies:

    .venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt

  5. Create the database and news cache table:

    .venv/bin/python manage.py migrate
.venv/bin/python manage.py createcachetable world_journal_cache

  6. Collect the static files used by both runserver and Waitress:

    .venv/bin/python manage.py collectstatic --noinput

  7. Start World Journal with your IANA timezone:

    TZ=Europe/Bucharest .venv/bin/python manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:8000 --noreload

    Or use Waitress for a machine that will keep the app running:

    TZ=Europe/Bucharest .venv/bin/python -m waitress --listen=0.0.0.0:8000 --threads=8 config.wsgi:application

  8. Open http://localhost:8000.

The terminal must remain open while the app is running. Press Ctrl+C when you want to stop it.

docs.title: Access from Other Devices
docs.text:
Find the host computer's IP address:

hostname -I

A device on the same trusted network can open an address such as http://192.168.1.15:8000. Everyone who can reach the server can access the shared app unless Authentication is enabled.

docs.title: Run Automatically on Boot
docs.text:
Create /etc/systemd/system/worldjournal.service and replace the username and project path:

[Unit]
Description=World Journal Waitress Server
After=network.target

[Service]
User=YOUR_LINUX_USERNAME
WorkingDirectory=/PATH/TO/YOUR/world-journal
Environment="TZ=Europe/Bucharest"
ExecStart=/PATH/TO/YOUR/world-journal/.venv/bin/python -m waitress --listen=0.0.0.0:8000 --threads=8 config.wsgi:application
Restart=always

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

Activate it:

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl start worldjournal
sudo systemctl enable worldjournal

Use sudo systemctl status worldjournal to inspect its state.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
Stop the server, open a terminal in the project folder and run:

git pull
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
.venv/bin/python manage.py migrate
.venv/bin/python manage.py createcachetable world_journal_cache
.venv/bin/python manage.py collectstatic --noinput

Start the server again and perform a hard refresh in the browser so updated static files are loaded.

Note: Export a backup from Settings > Backup before a major update. The app keeps personal data in db.sqlite3 and uploaded journal images in media/.

Read the Remote Access Guide Read the Authentication Guide

docs.title: Setup for Mac
docs.text:
1. Download and install Python 3.13.

    After installation, open the Python 3.13 folder in Applications and run Install Certificates.command.

  2. Open Terminal inside the folder where you want to keep the app.

  3. Clone the repository and enter the project folder:

    git clone https://github.com/mihail-pop/world-journal.git
cd world-journal

    If Git is not installed, macOS will offer to install the Command Line Developer Tools. Install them and run the command again.

  4. Create the virtual environment:

    python3 -m venv .venv

  5. Install the dependencies:

    .venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt

  6. Create the database and news cache table:

    .venv/bin/python manage.py migrate
.venv/bin/python manage.py createcachetable world_journal_cache

  7. Collect the static files used by both runserver and Waitress:

    .venv/bin/python manage.py collectstatic --noinput

  8. Start World Journal with your IANA timezone:

    TZ=Europe/Bucharest .venv/bin/python manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:8000 --noreload

    Or use Waitress for a machine that will keep the app running:

    TZ=Europe/Bucharest .venv/bin/python -m waitress --listen=0.0.0.0:8000 --threads=8 config.wsgi:application

  9. Open http://localhost:8000.

The Terminal window must remain open while the app is running. Press Control+C in that window when you want to stop it.

docs.title: Access from Other Devices
docs.text:
Hold Option and click the Wi-Fi icon to find the Mac's IP address. A device on the same trusted network can open an address such as http://192.168.1.15:8000.

Everyone who can reach the server can access the shared app unless Authentication is enabled.

docs.title: Run Automatically on Startup
docs.text:
Create ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.worldjournal.plist and replace /PATH/TO/YOUR/ with the real project path:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
    <key>Label</key>
    <string>com.worldjournal</string>
    <key>WorkingDirectory</key>
    <string>/PATH/TO/YOUR/world-journal</string>
    <key>EnvironmentVariables</key>
    <dict>
        <key>TZ</key>
        <string>Europe/Bucharest</string>
    </dict>
    <key>ProgramArguments</key>
    <array>
        <string>/PATH/TO/YOUR/world-journal/.venv/bin/python</string>
        <string>-m</string>
        <string>waitress</string>
        <string>--listen=0.0.0.0:8000</string>
        <string>--threads=8</string>
        <string>config.wsgi:application</string>
    </array>
    <key>RunAtLoad</key>
    <true/>
</dict>
</plist>

Load the service:

launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.worldjournal.plist

Use launchctl unload with the same path to stop automatic startup.

docs.title: Run Automatically on Boot
docs.text: The same service can run before login from /Library/LaunchDaemons/, but system daemons require ownership and permission changes. Use the login LaunchAgent unless the Mac is a dedicated server and you are comfortable managing launchd services.

docs.title: Setup for Windows
docs.text:
1. Download and install Python 3.13. During installation enable Add Python to PATH.

  2. Install Git for Windows, then open PowerShell in the folder where you want the app installed.

  3. Clone the repository and enter the project folder:

    git clone https://github.com/mihail-pop/world-journal.git
cd world-journal

  4. Create the virtual environment:

    python -m venv .venv

  5. Install the dependencies:

    .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.txt

  6. Create the database and news cache table:

    .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe manage.py migrate
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe manage.py createcachetable world_journal_cache

  7. Collect the static files used by both runserver and Waitress:

    .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe manage.py collectstatic --noinput

  8. Set your timezone for this terminal. Replace the example with your IANA timezone:

    $env:TZ="Europe/Bucharest"

  9. Start World Journal with Django:

    .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:8000 --noreload

    Or use Waitress for a machine that will keep the app running:

    .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m waitress --listen=0.0.0.0:8000 --threads=8 config.wsgi:application

  10. Open http://localhost:8000.

The terminal window must remain open while the app is running. Press Ctrl+C in that terminal when you want to stop it.

docs.title: Access from Other Devices
docs.text:
Run ipconfig and find the host computer's IPv4 address. A device on the same trusted network can then open an address such as http://192.168.1.15:8000.

Everyone who can reach the server can access the shared app unless Authentication is enabled.

docs.title: Run Automatically on Startup
docs.text:
Create run_world_journal.bat in the project folder and update the path:

@echo off
cd /d "C:\path\to\world-journal"
set TZ=Europe/Bucharest
set PY=.venv\Scripts\python.exe
%PY% manage.py migrate
%PY% manage.py createcachetable world_journal_cache
%PY% manage.py collectstatic --noinput
%PY% -m waitress --listen=0.0.0.0:8000 --threads=8 config.wsgi:application

Press Win+R, enter shell:startup and create a world_journal.vbs file there:

Set WshShell = CreateObject("WScript.Shell")
WshShell.Run """C:\path\to\world-journal\run_world_journal.bat""", 0
Set WshShell = Nothing

This starts the app after you log into Windows without leaving a terminal window open.

docs.title: Run Automatically on Boot
docs.text:
To start World Journal before login, install the batch file as a Windows service with a service manager such as NSSM:

winget install nssm
nssm install WorldJournal

Select run_world_journal.bat as the application path, install the service and start it with:

nssm start WorldJournal
